feedback.problem:
A quadratic equation in the variable $x$ with real coefficients has a root $x=-\frac{\sqrt{6}\,\text{i}}{4}.$ Given that the coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ in the equation is $16,$ find the equation. Write your answer in the form $a{x}^{2}+bx+c=0,$ where $a,$ $b,$ and $c$ are real constants.

{{field-1}}$=0$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the quadratic equation has real coefficients and $x=-\frac{\sqrt{6}\,\text{i}}{4}$ is a root, its conjugate $x=\frac{\sqrt{6}\,\text{i}}{4}$ must also be a root. Therefore, using the zero product property, we can write a quadratic equation with the required roots as follows:

$$
(x-\frac{\sqrt{6}\,\text{i}}{4})(x+\frac{\sqrt{6}\,\text{i}}{4})=0
$$

Multiplying out the parentheses and simplifying gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{(\frac{\sqrt{6}\,\text{i}}{4})}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-\frac{6}{16}(-1) & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+\frac{3}{8} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

This equation has roots $x=\pm \frac{\sqrt{6}\,\text{i}}{4},$ but the coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ is not $16.$ Therefore, to find the desired equation, we multiply the equation above by $16.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}16({x}^{2}+\frac{3}{8}) & =0 \\ 16{x}^{2}+6 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
